correctness.rationale: For S_{r,n}=K_r join independent n, r,n>=2, split by whether independent-side vertices receive any empty labels. The resulting two disjoint cases establish the candidate three-term formula. Independent literal-definition enumeration for all (r,n) in 2..4 with r+n<=7 matched every weight coefficient, total and minimum. The claimed minimum gamma=2 and count r^2+2 if n=2, else r^2, also follow from the formula. The symbolic case partition, not finite testing, establishes arbitrary r,n.

originality.rationale: FAIL: The candidate asserts S_{r,n} is not complete multipartite for r>=2. In fact S_{r,n}=K_{n,1,1,...,1}, with exactly r singleton parts and one part of size n. The already published Resultary finding All 2-rainbow dominating functions of complete multipartite graphs explicitly counts the same all-weight labeled functions by an exhaustive multinomial profile formula for every K_{n1,...,nk}; substitute (n,1,...,1) and collect profiles. Therefore the candidate is fully covered as a prior theorem specialization, even though the displayed algebraic form differs. The October 13 source overlooked a published October 4 result and its own asserted noncontainment is false.
residual_risks: The precise three-term factorization may not be printed verbatim in the prior paper, but the entire polynomial is already computable by its exact general formula; wording is not an originality distinction.
No scientific repair of a remaining original valuable theorem was supplied; publication must preserve the full failed source package.

value.rationale: FAIL: The closed polynomial is a convenient simplified specialization, but the exact invariant for the entire graph family is already determined by the published all-weight complete-multipartite theorem. Algebraic evaluation of its singleton-part profile sum supplies no motivated new structural boundary or mathematical gap, so the claimed new classification is a known result in different notation. Correct computation and reproducibility do not salvage value.
